children: China said Tuesday that the exporters must obtain approval to ship two drug-precursor chemicals to the U.S., Mexico, and Canada, a goodwill gesture ahead of a summit between the leaders of the world's two largest economies.
The controls come days before Chinese leader Xi Jinping is set to meet President Donald Trump in Washington, following repeated U.S. pressure on Beijing to disrupt the fentanyl supply chain.
The measures, announced by China's Commerce Ministry, took effect immediately.
China is a major source of fentanyl-precursor chemicals, which Mexican cartels use to produce the potent narcotic and smuggling into the U.S.
Beijing and Washington have stepped up joint efforts in recent years to curb the flow of those chemicals to North America.

In May, shortly after President Trump visited Beijing for talks with Xi, China imposed export controls on a different group of drug-precursor chemicals. The two leaders are expected to discuss fentanyl and a range of other when they meet in Washington later this week.
